text:
A rough Tuesday for some Microsoft 365 admins in Europe. According to The Register, some customers who reach Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Teams and Windows 365 Cloud PCs through Global Secure Access had trouble connecting on October 13. Microsoft's status update said part of the GSA infrastructure was performing below acceptable thresholds. The Register also noted it wasn't yet clear what caused it. I'm going by their reporting and Microsoft's updates, so please check the source for details.

The part that stuck with me is that the apps themselves may have been fine for people who weren't on that path. In my experience with Microsoft 365 and identity work, that kind of uneven impact makes the first hour of troubleshooting confusing. One person is stuck, and the person next to them is fine.

I'm still learning here. Next time, I might ask earlier how the affected users connect, not only which app is failing.

To anyone who spent that day fielding tickets or waiting on a status page, I hope things are calmer now. Anyone else have a favorite first question when only some users are affected?

#Microsoft365 #ITOperations #SystemsAdministration
why: Oct 13, 2026 Microsoft 365 outage affecting some European users on Global Secure Access, with a humble troubleshooting takeaway.

text:
Lately I've been brushing up on how conditional access works, and I'm realizing how much there still is to learn about it.

In my experience with identity and access management, it's easy to learn a setting by memorizing where the checkbox lives. It's harder to understand why a rule exists and what a user actually experiences when it triggers. I'm trying to slow down and think through the sign-in from the user's side before I think about the policy.

A few free things I've found useful for this kind of practice: the official Microsoft Learn modules, vendor-neutral Security+ study material, and just sketching a sign-in flow on paper. It's a little humbling how often my first sketch has a gap in it.

It's also okay to not have all of this figured out. Everyone was new at this once, and the tools keep changing, so most of us are learning on the move between tickets and busy weeks.

What has helped you understand identity concepts better? I'd love to hear about any resources, habits, or people who made it click for you.

#IdentityAndAccessManagement #Microsoft365 #ContinuousLearning
why: Sharing that he's brushing up on conditional access and identity concepts, and asking others what resources helped them.

text:
A quick thank-you to anyone who has ever worked a help desk queue.

In my experience with Microsoft 365 rollouts and identity and access work, the people answering the phone are usually the first to hear that something is wrong, and often the last to get credit when it's fixed. They also tend to talk to folks on their most stressful day, whether it's a locked account, a missing file, or a meeting that starts in two minutes.

A few things I'm still practicing myself:

- Assume the person on the other end is busy, not careless.
- Say "that sounds frustrating" before saying "try this."
- During an outage, a short, honest update is kinder than silence.
- When someone new asks a question, remember you once asked the same one.

If you're deep in an on-call week right now, I hope you get some real rest soon. It's okay not to have every answer.

What's one small thing a teammate did that made a hard day easier for you?

#ITSupport #HelpDesk #Mentorship
why: A gentle thank-you to help desk teams with simple tips on patience, outage kindness, and mentoring newcomers.

text:
Microsoft 365 admins had a small hiccup overnight. For a few hours, admins intermittently couldn't get into the Microsoft 365 admin center. I'm going by Microsoft's service health notes, which the University of Pennsylvania's IT team posts publicly.

As those notes describe it, Microsoft rolled its infrastructure back to a previous build and changed how the API responds to ease a surge of requests. They also turned off a recently introduced service change. The incident is marked restored.

It was short and I'm sure it was stressful for the people watching it. What stuck with me is how ordinary the fix was: undo the latest change, then figure out the rest. In my experience, that's good advice for any size of environment.

I'm still working on a related habit. When the admin portal won't load, do I know my second way in, and is it written down where a tired teammate can find it at 2 a.m.?

Hope your on-call week is going okay. How do you handle a plan B?

#Microsoft365 #ITOperations #SysAdmin
why: Short Oct 5-6, 2026 Microsoft 365 admin center access incident, resolved by rollback, with a takeaway about having a documented plan B.
